author: Ben DeCoste <bendecoste@gmail.com>
message:
Only show Keras API docs

Closes https://github.com/tf-encrypted/tf-encrypted/issues/587

Other docs are out of date right now.
This PR introduces the follwing:

* Started using [naploean](https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/extensions/napoleon.html).
  In short, napolean generates restructured text from google-style docstrings.
* Only show the keras API

There is one thing that I am not happy with, and that is that the titles generated
by sphinx-apidoc are bad.  E.g. for the `tf_encrypted.keras` page, the page title will be
`tf_encrypted.keras package`.  Where something like `Keras` or `TFE Keras` would be preferable.

Apparently using `-M` in the apidoc command should use the module title instead, but this does
not appear to be happening.

https://github.com/sphinx-doc/sphinx/pull/6492/ has introduced a `--template` command, which
we should be able to eventually leverage to fix the above issue.  Whether we want to wait or
take a different approach with this is up to us.  I can also manually edit the .rst files
and change the header if we want.  I just wanted to get a discussion going.

author: Benjamin DeCoste <bendecoste@gmail.com>
message:
Private compare & LSB (#190)

Implements private compare and LSB from secureNN.

The major changes are the functionality in securenn.py.  As well as large amounts of supporting work to make the various tensors required to implement the protocol work with each other.  

Most of this supporting work revolves around knowing how to lift a tensor properly depending on the type.  For example, pond.py can now know that if it is dealing with a private pond tensor with a prime backing, calling prot.mul(tensor, 2) will lift the 2 into a prime backed pond constant.

matrix multiplications.

We now have moved backed to requiring tensorflow 1.9.0 or greater!

message:
Only show Keras API docs

Closes https://github.com/tf-encrypted/tf-encrypted/issues/587

Other docs are out of date right now.
This PR introduces the follwing:

* Started using [naploean](https://www.sphinx-doc.org/en/master/usage/extensions/napoleon.html).
  In short, napolean generates restructured text from google-style docstrings.
* Only show the keras API

There is one thing that I am not happy with, and that is that the titles generated
by sphinx-apidoc are bad.  E.g. for the `tf_encrypted.keras` page, the page title will be
`tf_encrypted.keras package`.  Where something like `Keras` or `TFE Keras` would be preferable.

Apparently using `-M` in the apidoc command should use the module title instead, but this does
not appear to be happening.

https://github.com/sphinx-doc/sphinx/pull/6492/ has introduced a `--template` command, which
we should be able to eventually leverage to fix the above issue.  Whether we want to wait or
take a different approach with this is up to us.  I can also manually edit the .rst files
and change the header if we want.  I just wanted to get a discussion going.

author: j_c_cook <jack.cook@okstate.edu>
message:
Fix coaxial effective borehole resistance

The calculation has now been checked versus GLHEPRO, two errors were
found:

- The Reynolds number (Re) was improperly being calculated inside of the
  annulus, thus leading to improper convection coefficients and the
  resulting resistances inside of the annulus (contains inner and outer)

- The hyperbolic cotangent in the uniform borehole wall temperature
  effective resistance was not returning the proper value. This user
  believed that the function "arctanh" in numpy meant hyperbolic
  cotangent. Apparently, it does not. The solution is 1 divided by the
  "tanh" function.

author: j-c-cook <jack-c-cook@protonmail.com>
message:
Updates to utilities, boreholes and tilted example
- Remove the compute_angle_to() function in utilities and begin
  utilizing the np.arctan2 function. The only difference in usage is
  that the arctan2 function does not have an option for an origin
  placement, so the computed point must be shifted based on the origin.
- Add a `cardinal_point` function to utilities that requires a string
  as an input detailing the cardinal orientation. There are currently
  16 possible inputs, and each returns an angle in radians.
- Replace the "diamond" field in the tiled boreholes example with an
  optimal one from Eskilson (1987). Utilize the `cardinal_point`
  function for the orientation of boreholes in the custom example.
- Update note about availablity of solvers with tilted boreholes;
  now indicating that "detailed" and "similarities" is available.

message:
Refactor custom_borehole.py

The definition of each pipe type now has its own section in the script.
The mass flow is prescribed instead of the volume flow rate as is done in
the other examples. A mistake was corrected in the call to
`borehole_thermal_resistance()`: the borehole mass flow rate should be
provided (as opposed to the pipe mass flow rate). Pipes in single and
double U-tube boreholes are moved closer to the borehole wall and the
fluid is changed to propylene glycol 20%.

eliminates the for loop and is much more CPU efficient.

to be applicable independent of the solution method. Method-specific
tasks can be implemented in their own classes.

author: Jack Cook <jack.cook@okstate.edu>
message:
NewFeature unequal segment lengths (issue #135)

PR #136 introduces a `segment_lengths` parameter to the `gFunction`
class, supported by the addition of the attribute to the `Borehole`,
`_BasePipe`, and `Network` classes. This parameter enables a non-
uniform discretization of segments along the lengths of the boreholes
for calculations (including g-functions).

  - All g-function solvers are updated to support the feature. The
    identification of similarities had to be adjusted to verify that
	pairs of boreholes share the same discretization before applying
	thermal response factors to multiple pairs.
  - To conserve calculation speed in the evaluation of g-functions
    using equal segments or identical discretization along boreholes,
	`_equal_segment_ratios` and `_uniform_segment_ratios` boolean
	attributes are added to the `gFunction`class.
  - The ratio `1 / (2 * H_2)` is moved out of the integrand functions
    of the finite line source solution. `H_2` is now a vector and slows
	down the calculations if considered in `quad` and `quad_vec`.
  - A `segment_ratios()` function is added to the `utilities` module to
    facilitate the discretization of boreholes. Default parameters have
	been set to achieve acceptable accuracy. Issue #153 will determine
	optimal parameters for borehole discretization.
  - Tests are extended to cover the new features.

Co-authored-by: Massimo Cimmino <massimo.cimmino@polymtl.ca>
Co-authored-by: Jack Cook <jack.cook@okstate.edu>

author: j_c_cook <jack.cook@okstate.edu>
message:
Add pure water functionality to Fluid object

Coolprop provides access to incompresible mass-based binary
mixtures[1]. The string for the fluid mixture [2] appears as follows:
```
'INCOMP::Mixture-Percent%'
```
Where Mixture is replaced with a mixture to mix in with water [1] and
Percent is replaced with a value from 0-100. Although, there is an xmin
and xmax value for each mixture (shown in mixture table at [1]).

For pure water properties, the string becomes `'Water'` [3].

closes MassimoCimmino#75

[1]: http://www.coolprop.dreamhosters.com:8010/binaries/sphinx/fluid_properties/Incompressibles.html#pure
[2]: http://www.coolprop.dreamhosters.com:8010/binaries/sphinx/fluid_properties/Incompressibles.html#mixture-examples
[3]: http://www.coolprop.dreamhosters.com:8010/binaries/sphinx/fluid_properties/Incompressibles.html#mixture-examples

message:
Reformat pipes and networks

This is for #93, #100, and #125. `pipes` and `networks` modules are
reformatted.

- `numpy.dot()` and `numpy.linalg.multidot()` are replaced by the use of
the `@` operator introduced in [PEP465](https://www.python.org/dev/peps/pep-0465/).

- `numpy.asscalar()` is replaced by `array.item()` as recommended in the
`numpy` documentation as `asscalar` was deprecated in `v1.16`.

- Docstrings in `Pipe` and `Network` objects are reformatted to better
specify the expected types and array shapes of inputs and outputs to
functions and class methods.

author: Massimo Cimmino <massimo.cimmino@polymtl.ca>
message:
Initial implementation

`Network._network_coefficients_from_pipe_coefficients` is not very
efficient due to a triple `for` loop to evaluate matrix coefficients.
On top of this, it is very hard to read and understand, even alongside
the equations from the reference paper (Cimmino, 2019).

An alternate method is used here, starting from the coefficients of the
equation [Desired_variable(borehole)] = [a]*T_{in,borehole} + [b]*[T_b]
and taking into account the borehole connectivity to reduce to
[Desired_variable(borehole)] = [c]*T_{in,network} + [d]*[T_b].

The result is more efficient and much easier to read.

and `gfunction` modules. The variable name is now substituted with one of

confusion about the value to be provided.

Examples that make use of these modules are also updated.

author: Massimo Cimmino <massimo.cimmino@polymtl.ca>
message:
Initial implementation of optimized similarities

The optimized solver introduces an intermediate step in the identification
of similarities. Similarities between boreholes are checked first (we
assume that only similar pairs of boreholes contain similar pairs of
segments.

The integral in the finite line source (FLS) solution is now calculated
using `scipy.integrate.quad_vec` to speed up calculations. FLS solutions
at `r=r_b` is calculated separately from other distances because the
integrand functions have shapes that are too dissimilar (calculation time
increases if they are computed at the same time).

author: j-c-cook <jack.cook@okstate.edu>
message:
Modify functions to accept unequal segment lengths

The segments function in boreholes.py had previously only accounted for
the segment lengths to be equal on a specific borehole. This
modification provides the ability for the segments to have different
lengths.

The gfunction.py file needed to address unequal segment lengths in the
_map_axial_segment_pairs function so that the boreholes.segments
function could properly create bore segments. The _baseSolver object
had updates to the segment_lengths(), borehole_segments() and
_check_inputs() functions.

  - The summation of the segment lengths for each borehole are
    asserted to be within a tenth of a meter of the borehole height
  - The borehole_segments() function accesses the new variable
    segmentLengths (if its not None) to split boreholes into
    segments
  - The segment_lengths() function flattens the 2D segmentLengths list
    if segmentLengths is not None

author: Massimo Cimmino <massimo.cimmino@polymtl.ca>
message:
Add visualization features

The gFunction class can now plot the borehole temperatures and heat
extraction rates (both as a function of time and the profiles over the
length). These are often shown in publications and are useful to
interpret the result of g-function calculations.

In the past, modified versions of pygfunction were used to output these
for publications. The gFunction class and the new visualization methods
add this functionality natively while limiting the memory use through
the `profiles` options.

author: marmaduke woodman <marmaduke.woodman@univ-amu.fr>
message:
feat(hybrid-numba): disk-persistent JIT cache (§8.2)

Replace exec()-into-dict with _build_as_module(): renders generated source
to a real .py file under $TMPDIR/tvb_nb_hybrid_cache/, registers it in
sys.modules, then imports it. This gives Numba a real co_filename so that
cache=True on @nb.njit writes .nbi/.nbc native-code files next to the .py.

On second process startup with the same network topology the SHA-256 key
matches the existing .py, Numba loads the native cache directly (~50 ms vs
~5 s cold JIT). The in-process _COMPILED_FN_CACHE dict is retained as an
additional first-level fast path.

Changes:
- _build_as_module() helper with atomic os.replace write
- _build() delegates to _build_as_module instead of exec()
- NbHybridBackend.clear_cache() classmethod (in-process + disk)
- NbHybridBackend.get_cache_dir() staticmethod
- Template: cache=True added to all @nb.njit decorators (inline + plain)
- TestNbHybridDiskCache: 3 tests (dir created, in-process hit, clear)

models (n_modes=3).

author: FrancescaMelozzi <france.melozzi@gmail.com>
message:
TVB-1963: IMPLEMENT FCD ANALYZER

The aim of the code added here is:
calculating epochs of stability of the FCD using the spectral embedding
once identified the starting and the ending point of each epoch (epochs_extremes) the code calculates the FC of the timeseries belonging to that epoch
the first N eigenvector and the first N eigenvalues for each FC are extracted (I set N=3, num_eig=3, but it could be a parameter that the user can set)

I set also mode and var = 0 since I don't know which is a cleaver way to store the results (eigenvalues and eigenvectors) in case of mode>1  var>1

The Analyzer gives no errors in the GUI (if used with timeseries, but it gives errors if used with BOLD signals), however it does not return nothing (I did not set what it should return since I don't understand really how it works)

If the FCD is small (short timeseries or larger sw or sp) the spectral embedding is not able to find the epochs_extremes and I think the code will give errors...we should prevent this error by advising to use FCD of right dimension (I don't know which is the minimum size but I can figure it)

author: Marmaduke Woodman <marmaduke.woodman@univ-amu.fr>
message:
add example autograd member primitive

TVB implements most arithmetic in class members, while autograd is
expecting free standing functions.  Forunately, this can be resolved
by delaying primitive & vjp registration after instantiation of the
object.

This is doubly useful because it will ensure that we can specialize the
vjp operator for the runtime use case and not rely on general cases.
When most parameters are constant, this will greatly simplify the
calculation of vjp as those constants do not need to be handled.

Specializing on a per object basis may bloat autograd's registry a bit
but ensures that if the model is instantiated more than once, the
appropriate vjp will be generated and used.

author: Marmaduke Woodman <marmaduke.woodman@univ-amu.fr>
message:
initial startup speed-up

When just trying to write unit tests and run them, the startup time of
the library is slow enough to get distracted (8.2 s on i5 SSD Mac).
Looking at the extensive log output, I saw enough delay between warnings
of different models to realize that importing all models is causing this
delay.

I then commented the imports of tvb.simulator.models.__init__ and saw
startup time drop to 0.5 s.  I would guess that this speed drop is due
to the gufunc or neotraits class registration, not yet sure which.

The current fix is breaking code such as

     from tvb.simulator.models import Linear

so it would be useful to resolve the underlying problem *or* implement
a lazy loading approach, since, at runtime, only one model is usually
in use; loading all is excessive.

  state_variable_dfuns codegen attributes

  ZerlautAdaptationFirstOrder (5 svars, erfc transfer function pipeline)

author: marmaduke woodman <marmaduke.woodman@univ-amu.fr>
message:
feat(hybrid-numba): add SubSample, SpatialAverage, Projection, Bold monitors (M2-M5)

All monitors implemented as Python-side post-processing in _apply_monitors():

M2 - SubSample: period enforcement via time-point masking, selecting chunks
     whose mid-time falls within dt/2 of a period boundary.

M3 - SpatialAverage: node grouping via spatial_mean matrix (n_areas, n_nodes)
     applied with einsum to reduce node dimension.

M4 - Projection (EEG/MEG/iEEG): gain-matrix projection from node space to
     sensor space. Handles mode summation and adds singleton mode dim.

M5 - Bold: HRF convolution via rolling stock buffer with interim accumulation.
     Stateful across multiple run_network() calls via _nb_ prefixed attrs.
     Supports FirstOrderVolterra k1/V0 scaling.

Tests: 7 new monitor tests covering shape, values, period spacing, and
statefulness. Updated test_unsupported_monitor_raises to use ProgressLogger.

175 tests total, all passing.

author: Omar Nassar <nassar.omarr@gmail.com>
message:
improve speed of reduced set models

Reduced Set models don't use numba for enhanced performance. This uses numba njit wrapper to compile the deriviative functions during runtime, and provide considerable performance gain.

Since numba currently doesn't fully support jit-ed classes, derivative functions have to move outside the class scope. To improved readability, they were moved to a new file: _dfun_stefanescu_jirsa.py.

To test the changes a new unit test module was added: models_benchmark.py. Here, we compute the derivative multiple times within a time window with/without numba and compare the throughput. Around 5x performance gains were observed. We also verify that numba doesn't change derivative values.

message:
test(hybrid-numba): add integrative Python-vs-Numba monitor comparison tests

Each test runs the same simulation through both the Python hybrid
step-loop and the Numba backend, applies the same monitor logic,
and asserts numerical equivalence at rtol=1e-2:

- TemporalAverage (chunk_size=1 and chunk_size=5)
- SubSample (step-based period masking, matching Python istep semantics)
- GlobalAverage (mean across nodes)
- SpatialAverage (spatial_mean matrix grouping)
- Projection/EEG (gain-matrix sensor projection)
- Bold (HRF convolution with FirstOrderVolterra scaling)

Bug fix: SubSample mask changed from float time-point rounding to
step-based modular arithmetic to avoid float32 precision artifacts.

182 tests total, all passing.

The FCD calculator now gives at output= FCD, FCDsegmented, eigenvectors of the FC calculated over the epoch of the FCD.
FCDsegmented is a matrix that helps the visualization of the epochs of stability identified in the algorithm. FCD segmented is the FCD but with value 1.1 to the entries that don't belong to the epoch of stability.

The first epoch of stability is always neglected.

If the epochs are not found, the code gives as output the first 3 eigenvector of the global FC (FC calculated over the entire time of the timeseries)
The code works with TimeSeriesRegion

The eigenvectors and the eigenvalues are extracted only for mode=0, var=0

author: Marmaduke Woodman <mmwoodman@gmail.com>
message:
coupling template w/ unit and integration tests

Monolithic templates are hard to debug, while small templates don't
compose well because the template engine doesn't understand data flow
and semantics in the generate code.  The compromise, which this commit
adds an example of, is to have the units of templates correspond to
functions in the target language, with a unit test verifying the
function in isolation (with  a trivial wrapper kernel), and an
integration test which uses in function in a full simulation kernel.

M3 projection monitors), combined-mode dfun generation for

calling opencode run with zai/glm-5.1 to add coupling_terms, parameter_names,
dfun_intermediates, state_variable_dfuns. Includes validation (attr existence,
key matching, coupling_term usage, parameter attribute check) and 3-retry

author: marmaduke woodman <marmaduke.woodman@univ-amu.fr>
message:
feat(hybrid-numba): Sigmoidal cfun + JansenRit model support

Add Sigmoidal and SigmoidalJansenRit coupling functions to the numba
hybrid backend, and support the JansenRit model as a second model target
alongside MontbrioPazoRoxin and KIonEx.

Backend changes (nb_hybrid.py):
- _cfun_type(): recognise Sigmoidal -> 'sigmoidal', SigmoidalJR -> 'sigmoidal_jr'
- _cfun_params(): return float32[5] array (replaces (cfun_a, cfun_b) 2-tuple)
  Layout: [a, sigma, midpoint, cmin, cmax] for Sigmoidal;
          [a, e0, r, v0, 0] for SigmoidalJansenRit
- _check_compatibility(): accept JansenRit alongside MPR and KIonEx
- _run_compiled(): pass cfun_params array (single arg per projection)

Template changes (nb-hybrid-sim.py.mako):
- cfun_a/cfun_b scalar args -> cfun_params float32[5] array throughout
- Pre-cfun hook inside CSR inner loop for sigmoidal_jr (pre-synaptic
  sigmoid on source state values before weighted-sum accumulation)
- Post-cfun dispatch: sigmoidal branch added; linear/scaling use cfun_params[0/1]
- Both mono_src (n_modes==1) and general paths updated

Model changes (jansen_rit.py):

author: Marmaduke Woodman <marmaduke.woodman@univ-amu.fr>
message:
add example autograd member primitive

TVB implements most arithmetic in class members, while autograd is
expecting free standing functions.  Forunately, this can be resolved
by delaying primitive & vjp registration after instantiation of the
object.

This is doubly useful because it will ensure that we can specialize the
vjp operator for the runtime use case and not rely on general cases.
When most parameters are constant, this will greatly simplify the
calculation of vjp as those constants do not need to be handled.

Specializing on a per object basis may bloat autograd's registry a bit
but ensures that if the model is instantiated more than once, the
appropriate vjp will be generated and used.

This commit just adds a test case showing how this can be done.

message:
feat(hybrid-numba): checkpointing, mode_map tests, code quality (§8.8/8.9/8.10)

§8.8 Resumable runs / snapshot API:
- CompiledNetworkFn.run(return_snapshot=True) -> (outputs, snapshot)
  snapshot = {'states': [...], 'buffers': {...}}; captured from in-place
  Numba writes, zero kernel changes required
- CompiledNetworkFn.resume(snapshot, nstep) restores state+buffers and
  continues; numerically identical to a single longer run
- _run_compiled gains _initial_buffers=None parameter

§8.9 Testing gaps:
- TestNbHybridModeMap (4 tests): non-identity mode_map on 2-mode MPR nets;
  verifies accepted, shape, finite, and that mixing actually differs from identity
- TestNbHybridLargeNScaling (2 tests): N=100 no-error smoke test; N=50
  speedup regression (cached Numba vs Python loop with generous bound)

§8.10 Code quality:
- __all__ added to nb_hybrid.py (NbHybridBackend, CompiledNetworkFn,
  NetworkAnalysis, SubnetworkInfo, ProjectionInfo)
- backend/__init__.py: lazy __getattr__ for NbHybridBackend + CompiledNetworkFn
  (direct import caused circular dep via integrators -> equations -> backend)
- Plan doc: §8.3 marked DONE, §6 table extended, Phase C2 added to §7

message:
first sketch of symbolic jacobians

symbolic jacobians are in reach for most of our models,
especially with the upcoming DSL.  this is a first
sketch which computes derivatives symbolically with
sympy for Jansen Rit and generates a sequences of
instructions which can be strung together, eval'd and
then jit'd with numba.

one could then also specialize when parameter values
are known by substituting the values in prior to
doing the symbolics, which will help as well.

author: marmaduke woodman <marmaduke.woodman@univ-amu.fr>
message:
fix(kionex): log(a/b) -> log(a)-log(b) in ionic current helpers

Replace log(K_o/K_i) and log(Na_o/Na_i) with log(K_o)-log(K_i) and
log(Na_o)-log(Na_i) in all four representation sites:

  - dfun_helpers strings (used by nb-hybrid-sim codegen)
  - _numpy_dfun inner helper lambdas
  - standalone @njit I_K_form / I_Na_form (two duplicate copies)

In float32 the ratio K_o/K_i can underflow to zero before the log is
taken, yielding -inf.  Computing log(a)-log(b) avoids the intermediate
ratio and keeps both operands in the normal float32 range as long as each
concentration is individually representable.

Note: log(Cl_o0/Cl_i0) is left as-is because both values are compile-time
constants that are always positive and finite.

Also document in TestNbHybridMprKIonEx.test_output_shapes that NaN-freedom
for KIonEx in float32 is a separate open item (K_o can go negative under
extreme states), while the Python float64 path is already checked in
test_mpr_kionex.py.

author: marmaduke woodman <marmaduke.woodman@univ-amu.fr>
message:
feat(hybrid-numba): add ReducedWongWang, Epileptor, WilsonCowan, G2D; strip CSR zeros

Model codegen attributes added (coupling_terms, parameter_names,
dfun_intermediates, state_variable_dfuns):
- ReducedWongWang (wong_wang.py): 1 svar S, 8 params, 2 intermediates
  (x_ww, H_ww); S clipped to [0,1] via existing boundaries
- Epileptor (epileptor.py): 6 svars, 16 params, 4 ternary intermediates
  (f1, zterm, h, f2); modification=False only
- WilsonCowan (wilson_cowan.py): 2 svars E/I, 22 params, 4 intermediates
  (x_e, x_i, s_e, s_i); shifted sigmoid (shift_sigmoid=True only)
- Generic2dOscillator (oscillator.py): already added in prior session

Backend (nb_hybrid.py):
- _check_compatibility: accept RWW, Epileptor, WilsonCowan (7 models total)
- Per-model constraint checks: rejects Epileptor(modification=True) and
  WilsonCowan(shift_sigmoid=False) with NotImplementedError
- _build_projection_info: strip structural epsilon zeros via
  eliminate_zeros() on a copy of p.weights before extracting
  .data/.indices/.indptr; idelays aligned with stripped structure

Tests (test_nb_hybrid.py):
- TestNbHybridReducedWongWang: 4 tests (accepted, shape, finite, py-match)
- TestNbHybridEpileptor: 4 tests
- TestNbHybridWilsonCowan: 4 tests (uses source_cvar=[0] for E-only coupling)
- test_rejects_unsupported_model: updated to use SupHopf (WilsonCowan now accepted)
- 283 tests passing total (was 52)

author: marmaduke woodman <marmaduke.woodman@univ-amu.fr>
message:
feat(hybrid-numba): add Kuramoto, Difference, HyperbolicTangent, PreSigmoidal cfuns

All 9 hybrid coupling functions now supported:
- Linear, Scaling, Sigmoidal, SigmoidalJansenRit (existing)
- Kuramoto: a * sin(x) post-hook
- Difference: a * x (maps to scaling internally)
- HyperbolicTangent: a * (1 + tanh((x-midpoint)/sigma)) pre-hook
- PreSigmoidal: H * (Q + tanh(G*(P*x - theta))) pre-hook

Template fix: pre-cfun transforms moved outside CSR accumulation loop
to match Python pipeline (weighted sum -> pre -> scale -> post).
This also fixes sigmoidal_jr correctness for heterogeneous source states.

_cfun_params array expanded from 5 to 8 elements for new parameter layouts.
6 new tests in TestNbHybridCfunExtended (all python-vs-numba comparisons).
151 tests total, all passing.

author: Mathieu Brédif <mathieu.bredif@ign.fr>
message:
refactor(renderer): LayeredMaterial splitted and simplified

Worid has been fone to simplify LayeredMaterial and its surrounding
parts, especially with the management of textures in shaders.

LayeredMaterial has been splitted, and has now a LayeredMaterialLayer
property: this object will contain the textures linked to the material,
and uniforms related to each material.

Uniforms from LayeredMaterial are no longer accessible as is, and should
be accessible with directly using the uniform name. The material does
not do a lot of things, apart attaching a layer to it and managing
uniforms.

TileMesh has been simplified, removing all accessors in favor of direct
access to its properties. Material operations that were executed in it
have also been removed.

Shaders have been rewritten to reflect change quoted above. In an
attempt to simplify things and make them more comprehensible, TileFS and
TileVS have been splitted in multiple chunks, which are installed
through ShaderChunk.install.

BREAKING CHANGES: the API of TileMesh and LayeredMaterial have changed.
BREAKING CHANGES: LayeredMaterialConstants and RendererConstant have
been removed.

message:
feat(style): add Style inheritance

It is now possible to specify a `Style` parent for another `Style`. That
way, it is possible to define a global `Style` for a `ColorLayer`, while
defining one with property specific to a `FeatureGeometry` for example.
The `Style` of the `FeatureGeometry` will then only have the minimum
requirement, and it will read missing properties from its parent. It is
a dynamic reading, so it the parent values are changing, it is changing
as well for the child style.

This is a proposition for improvement in #1318.

BREAKING CHANGE: `Style#text.halo` is not available anymore, and each
property of it as been place in the `text` object, with the `halo`
prefix: `haloWidth`, `haloColor` and `haloBlur`.

author: Augustin Trancart <augustin.trancart@oslandia.com>
message:
Chore: deduplicate dependencies between itowns.js and debug.js

If you import things somewhere in bundles itowns.js AND debug.js,
corresponding files (and all their deps) are getting bundled twice.
Apart from the extra size, this can cause bugs when some deps (eg.
three.js) expects you to include them only once (for id counting for
instance).

This commit removes deps that are already in itowns.js from debug.js.
One consequences is that we need to include debug.js after itowns.js.

In the future, it would be good to also extract a vendor.js bundle.

author: Thomas Broyer <t.broyer@ltgt.net>
message:
Build using webpack, getting dependencies with NPM

Notable changes:
 * Replace src/ThirdParty/ entirely with NPM dependencies
 * Replace many src/Renderer/Three/ and src/Renderer/ThreeExtented
   scripts with scripts coming right from the Three.js module.
   Those are a bit hackish though, as they modify the THREE object;
   use with care.
 * Make all implicit dependencies on Three.js explicit by adding a

        var THREE = require('three');

   at the top of the files, or adding 'three' to the AMD dependencies.
 * Add aliases in Webpack to avoid rewriting many dependencies.
   Cleanup will be done in a forthcoming change.
 * Replace require-text with Webpack's raw-loader. This is configured
   as a rule for all *.glsl files, rather than on each import.
 * src/Renderer/Utils.js won't work as it "depends" on a "Cartography"
   module that doesn't exist. The import has been moved to the top of
   the file, but commented out so that Webpack doesn't complain.

Add earlyDropFunction attribute to Commands (#94)

Allow the user to specify a function to decide if a Command
must be cancelled.

Note that children creation commands are tagged as non-cancellable.
That's because children creation only happens when a node has no children.

If 1 of the child creation request is cancelled the node
will be in an invalid state: 3 children and no way to create
the last one.

Fix #82 'Tiles are not displayed'

author: Augustin Trancart <augustin.trancart@oslandia.com>
message:
chore(build): drop babel-plugin-webpack-loader

babel-plugin-webpack-loader allowed to use webpack loaders in babel to
transpile our sources. This commit changes the approach:
- it lets babel deals with ES6 modules when it runs alone
- it uses babel-plugin-inline-import to import json and glsl (this was
  done by webpack raw-loader before)

The consequence of that is that glsl and json are now handled by babel
instead of webpack. I believe this won't change anything.

We have now a slightly more complex webpack.config.js, but we removed
some copy-pasta and some magic, leading to a simpler config overall.

The fact we no more pass through webpack at each babel invocation gives
us some nice perf improvement:
- `npm run transpile` execution time is divided by 2 on my machine
- `npm run test-unit` execution time divided by 3.

that will be visible. This reduces network/mem usage, for the same visual
result.

message:
feat(core): allow layer to specify which elements should be updatable

Some layers use separated objects for metadata and drawable objects.
For instance PointCloudProvider or 3dTilesProvider.

Attached layers (e.g texture layers) expect to receive a drawable object,
in their update function.

So this commit adds an optional metadataToElements function to layers,
allowing them to returns the to-be-updated object from metadata, and
its parent.

message:
Add earlyDropFunction attribute to Commands (#94)

Allow the user to specify a function to decide if a Command
must be cancelled.

Note that children creation commands are tagged as non-cancellable.
That's because children creation only happens when a node has no children.

If 1 of the child creation request is cancelled the node
will be in an invalid state: 3 children and no way to create
the last one.

Fix #82 'Tiles are not displayed'

message:
Fix race condition in the initialisation of the Scene.

Doing Quadtree.init with the geometry layer triggers and update of the
scene, which later causes subdivision to be made to the first 3 levels.
When this subdivision is made, we want to be absolutely sure that
LayerConfiguration is complete. Otherwise, layers textures won't be
downloaded if they are added after this initialisation.

FYI, this race conditions was triggered (most of the time) in Firefox but not in chromium.

> For type "MultiPoint", the "coordinates" member is an array of positions.

Before that, we were considering that the `coordinates` member was an
array of array of positions.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
refactor(gis): remove _internalUnitStorage from Coordinates/Extent

_internalUnitStorage was initially introduced in fc6bc1a0f8d75edba03d to be
able to store coordinates using EPSG:4326 but with radians angles to avoid
too many conversions degrees <-> radians.

While this possibility is useful, it also introduces a tricky issue where
2 Coordinates with the same 'crs' might not use the same internal representation.
(see https://github.com/iTowns/itowns/pull/690, or https://github.com/iTowns/itowns/pull/664
for recent fixes related to this).

This PR removes _internalUnitStorage completely and instead introduces a custom
EPSG code (EPSG:4326:R) when using 4326 with Radians.

author: pierre-eric <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
feature: add StaticProvider to download from a list of predefined images

Allows to use iTowns features without the trouble of setting up a WM(T)S server.

Given a metadata json file like this:

{
  'file1.png': [west1, east1, south1, north1],
  'file2.png': [west2, east2, south2, north2],
  ...
  'fileN.png': [westN, eastN, southN, northN]
}

The StaticProvider will simply find the best image for a given tile (= the image
with the smallest extent covering all of the tile's extent).

author: Gerald Choqueux <gerald.choqueux@ign.fr>
message:
refactor(core): use common geometry in meshTile

 * identical geometries are reused to build the tileMeshs
 * the bounding boxes is calculated by THREE.js
 * bounding boxes can use the Parent's worldMatrix (tile).

BREAKING CHANGE
The geodesic normal in the center of the tile's geometry is aligned with the mesh's local Z axis.
Previously, the tiles were not oriented. their local landmark had the same orientation as the world landmark. You must take into account the orientation of the tile if you add objects to this tile.

Fixes:
 * Ellipsoid tile: The tile's geometry normal is computed with correct geodesic normal
 * reduces obb calculation errors see #87 issues
 * errors obb/culling for pano tile

Performance
 * the processes time (to build tiles in TileProvider.executeCommand) and used memory (geometryTile) are divided by ~3

author: Augustin Trancart <augustin.trancart@oslandia.com>
message:
Fix race condition in the initialisation of the Scene.

Doing Quadtree.init with the geometry layer triggers and update of the
scene, which later causes subdivision to be made to the first 3 levels.
When this subdivision is made, we want to be absolutely sure that
LayerConfiguration is complete. Otherwise, layers textures won't be
downloaded if they are added after this initialisation.

FYI, this race conditions was triggered (most of the time) in Firefox but not in chromium.

be used directly, so it's kept in the cache (no need to replace it).

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
refactor(core): change view.notifyChange semantics

This commit changes the semantics of view.notifyChange function to something more
useful:
  changeSource now drives layer update.

This implies that no changeSource -> no update.

'changeSource' can be either a layer, an object from a layer or the camera.

The signature also changed slightly:
   notifyChange(needsRedraw = false, changeSource = undefined)
becomes:
   notifyChange(changeSource = undefined, needsRedraw = true)

Some examples usage:
  - notifyChange(): the scene will be redraw, but no update will be performed. This
is useful if a user adds some objetcs to the scene and wants to request a redraw but
do no need a full update of all layer (eg: a measure tool drawn with threejs lines)
  - notifyChange(XXX): only the layer XXX (or the layer to which XXX belongs) will
be updated. So if you have 100 layers, and layer #4 has a new texture, it will not
cause a full update of other layers.
  - notifyChange(camera): this is equivalent to the previous notifyChange(true): all
layers will be updated.

MainLoop also handles changeSource filtering and could later even handle ancestor
lookup (if we build a common ancestor lookup interface).

BREAKING CHANGE: change view.notifyChange signature and semantics

Fixes #768

BREAKING CHANGE:
Before this change, `view.addLayer` was throwing some errors directly in
some cases, and rejecting the promise in others. This replaces the
former for the latter in all cases. If you relied on a try/catch block
surrounding `view.addLayer` to catch some undocumented errors, you need
to move your error handling code to your promise rejection handler.

author: pierre-eric <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
feat (core): only use threeJsLayer feature when necessary

Using three.js' layers visibility has a big drawback: we're limited to 31 visibility
groups.
It's quite a low amount, so this commit changes the approach used for visibility:
  - GeometryLayer uses 'layer.object3d.visible' instead
  - layers attached to GeomLayer (like the TileDebug one) still use threeJsLayer,
    because their elements are attached to another layer's objects so they don't
    all share a common parent

Another change included is that now it doesn't make sense to use view.scene as a
default object3d parameter, so this commit switches to a Group instead.

message:
refactor (3dtiles): don't instanciate several TextDecoder at startup

This commit changes the way 3dtiles support code uses TextDecoder.
Instead of instancing 1 TextDecoder per file on startup, we only create
one in 3dTiles_Provider and use it everywhere.

It ease unit testing (avoid the need to polyfill TextDecoder in node context when
3dtiles isn't tested) and as a side effect should reduce startup time and mem usage.

author: Augustin Trancart <augustin.trancart@oslandia.com>
message:
Fix race condition in the initialisation of the Scene.

Doing Quadtree.init with the geometry layer triggers and update of the
scene, which later causes subdivision to be made to the first 3 levels.
When this subdivision is made, we want to be absolutely sure that
LayerConfiguration is complete. Otherwise, layers textures won't be
downloaded if they are added after this initialisation.

FYI, this race conditions was triggered (most of the time) in Firefox but not in chromium.

If there are `stops` in any property of the Style, they will be taken

Note that this is a partial support, as the Mapbox Style specs have evolved:
https://docs.mapbox.com/mapbox-gl-js/style-spec/expressions

This commit is also moving a lot of things that were in
`VectorTileParser` back to `VectorTilesSource`, to keep things more
independant.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric@damsy.net>
message:
refactor(gis): remove _internalUnitStorage from Coordinates/Extent (#693)

_internalUnitStorage was initially introduced in fc6bc1a0f8d75edba03d to be
able to store coordinates using EPSG:4326 but with radians angles to avoid
too many conversions degrees <-> radians.

While this possibility is useful, it also introduces a tricky issue where
2 Coordinates with the same 'crs' might not use the same internal representation.
(see https://github.com/iTowns/itowns/pull/690, or https://github.com/iTowns/itowns/pull/664
for recent fixes related to this).

This PR removes _internalUnitStorage completely and instead introduces a custom
EPSG code (EPSG:4326:R) when using 4326 with Radians.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
Implement different layer update strategies

Add a configuration option to specify what kind of update strategy
is applied for a given level.

This commits implements 4:
  * STRATEGY_MIN_NETWORK_TRAFFIC: minimize network traffic by always
fetching the texture level matching node's level. This is the default
strategy.
  * STRATEGY_GROUP: maps level to groups. This effectively reduces the
granularity of a given layer. Was previously implemented in TileMesh
for elevation.
  * PROGRESSIVE: this strategy progressively refine level. Increment is
configurable (default: 1)
  * DICHOTOMY: is a special case of PROGRESSIVE.

author: pierre-eric <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
feat(core): implement layer priorities

Before this commit, commands issued by layers were stored per-host.
These commands queues are sorted by commands priority.

The problem caused by this design is that commands priority values
are not normalized and if 2 different types of layer (eg: color and pointcloud)
shared the same host, their commands ended up in the same queue.
Their ordering would be determined by comparing "apples and oranges": color
layer priorities are not comparable to pointcloud layer priorities.

To address this problem, this commit introduces 1 queue per layer
within the same host and adds an optional layer priority.

When the scheduler has an empty slot for a given host, it will first
select the layer (based on their relative priorities) and then pick
its top most command.

author: Adrien Berthet <berthet.a@gmail.com>
message:
fix(source): set the Style.minzoom correctly in VectorTilesSource

The previous behavior was as follow:
- check the presence of `minzoom` for a specific layer
- if it is not present, use `2` has a default value
- insert this value to the `stops` array
The resulting problem is that if `minzoom` is not defined and the first
`stop` value was greater than 2, it was still adding a `2 to first stop`
step.

A solution has been added here, to consider that the `minzoom` is either
the specified minzoom, or whichever is the highest between 2 and the
littlest `stop`.

of this update being fired.

Now the source of notifyChange() calls are stored, and the layer.preUpdate()

now start at the common ancestor (if any) of all the notifyChanges() sources.

author: Adrien Berthet <adrien.berthet@ign.fr>
message:
refacto(provider): make DataSourceProvider more modulable

Rewrite the `executeCommand` method of the DataSourceProvider to accept
three way of receiving data:
- by fetching it, parsing it and converting it in the provider
- by giving fetched data to the layer and parsing it and converting it
  in the provider
- by giving parsed data to the layer and converting it in the provider

And thus FileSource can be simplified drastically and extended to
receive ANY type of data, not only geojson, kml and gpx.

preprocessLayer. This *will* get asynchronous in the future when we'll
support GetCapabilities call and other metadata fetching methods.

author: pierre-eric <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
refactor(core): unify SSE computation methods

Until this commit each geometry type had its own SSE computation methods.
The goal of this commit is to provide a single method based on:
  - bounding-box (BB)
  - geometricError (in meters)
  - distance

The computation is simple:
  - transform camera in BB's basis
  - compute distance camera - BB
  - project geometricError on screen at distance

The last step produce a screen-space-error in pixels.

Geometric error values depend on the data type:
  - 3dtiles: the tileset defines a geometricError per node so we can use this value
  - pointcloud: PotreeConverter defines a spacing, which is the average distance
between points in each node. We use: geometricError = spacing / 2^depth
  - tiles: this commit adapted the existing formula to use consistent units

author: Augustin Trancart <augustin.trancart@oslandia.com>
message:
Change import path from absolute to relative

This change is a necessary step to allow client code to import our
modules directly.

To achieve this, I used a little python script. I also had to change
some import orders to make the linter happy.

Work on generating lib/ and inlining glsl will be done in a subsequent
commit.

For reference, here is the python script:

import glob
import os
import re
import fileinput

prefix=os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'src')
list = ('Core', 'Globe', 'MobileMapping', 'Renderer', 'Scene')

for filename in glob.glob(prefix + '/**/*.js', recursive=True):
    for line in fileinput.input(filename, inplace=True):
        # check if local import
        if line.startswith('import ') and any(word in line for word in list):
            search = re.search('import (.*) from \'(.*)\';', line)
            if search:
                # importing a js
                importString = search.group(1)
                import_abs_path = os.path.join(prefix, search.group(2))
                import_rel_path = os.path.relpath(import_abs_path, os.path.dirname(filename))
                if not import_rel_path.startswith('.'):
                    # webpack needs ./ before relative path
                    import_rel_path = './' + import_rel_path
                print('import ' + importString + ' from \'' + import_rel_path + '\';')
            else:
                # importing something else
                print(line, end='')
        else:
            # import from node_modules
            print(line, end='')

message:
feat (core): complete and use FrameRequesters

This commit adds eight moments when a `FrameRequester` can be called in the
MainLoop :
- `UPDATE_START`
- `BEFORE_CAMERA_UPDATE`
- `AFTER_CAMERA_UPDATE`
- `BEFORE_LAYER_UPDATE`
- `AFTER_LAYER_UPDATE`
- `BEFORE_RENDER`
- `AFTER_RENDER`
- `UPDATE_END`

They can be used like this anywhere (at least where a view is reachable):
`view.addFrameRequester(itowns.View.BEFORE_CAMERA_UPDATE, frameRequester);`
where `frameRequester` is a function.

They are removed following a similar process:
`view.removeFrameRequester(itowns.View.BEFORE_CAMERA_UPDATE, frameRequester);`.

In the MainLoop, they are triggered each time (according to where they
belong) using
`view.execFrameRequesters(itowns.View.BEFORE_CAMERA_UPDATE);`.

Replace two cases where FrameRequesters weren't used, in `globe.js` with
`onAfterRender` and in `layersColorVisible.html` with `preRender`.
Adapt two cases where FrameRequesters were being used.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
refactor(gis): remove _internalUnitStorage from Coordinates/Extent

_internalUnitStorage was initially introduced in fc6bc1a0f8d75edba03d to be
able to store coordinates using EPSG:4326 but with radians angles to avoid
too many conversions degrees <-> radians.

While this possibility is useful, it also introduces a tricky issue where
2 Coordinates with the same 'crs' might not use the same internal representation.
(see https://github.com/iTowns/itowns/pull/690, or https://github.com/iTowns/itowns/pull/664
for recent fixes related to this).

This PR removes _internalUnitStorage completely and instead introduces a custom
EPSG code (EPSG:4326:R) when using 4326 with Radians.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
test: use puppeteer to test all examples

This commit replaces the itowns-testing.js hack with puppeteer (https://github.com/GoogleChrome/puppeteer).

Advantages:
  - a real browser (Chrome) instead of node + mocks for missing features
  - WebGL capable
  - Can take screenshots and save them (not used on Travis yet)
  - Debuggable using Chrome Dev tools (Chrome instance used by puppeteer can be headless or not)

Each example now have at least one test to verify we can open it and that it
reaches the "mainloop has finished running" state.

I also implemented a couple tests for other examples (see 3dtiles and globe).

Adding test is easy, and we could add more to exercise more parts of itowns.

Last but not least: with this change the separation of examples in 2 files (html + js) is
not needed anymore.

author: gchoqueux <gerald.choqueux@ign.fr>
message:
refactor(renderer): LayeredMaterial splitted and simplified

Worid has been fone to simplify LayeredMaterial and its surrounding
parts, especially with the management of textures in shaders.

LayeredMaterial has been splitted, and has now a LayeredMaterialLayer
property: this object will contain the textures linked to the material,
and uniforms related to each material.

Uniforms from LayeredMaterial are no longer accessible as is, and should
be accessible with directly using the uniform name. The material does
not do a lot of things, apart attaching a layer to it and managing
uniforms.

TileMesh has been simplified, removing all accessors in favor of direct
access to its properties. Material operations that were executed in it
have also been removed.

Shaders have been rewritten to reflect change quoted above. In an
attempt to simplify things and make them more comprehensible, TileFS and
TileVS have been splitted in multiple chunks, which are installed
through ShaderChunk.install.

BREAKING CHANGES: the API of TileMesh and LayeredMaterial have changed.
BREAKING CHANGES: LayeredMaterialConstants and RendererConstant have
been removed.

author: pierre-eric <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
refactor(core): unify mesh picking methods

The idea of this PR is to expose a single entry point for querying the view.

This method belongs to the View.

Here are a few example usage:
  * view.pickObjectsAt({ x, y })
  * view.pickObjectsAt({ x, y }, 'wfsBuilding')
  * view.pickObjectsAt({ x, y }, 'wfsBuilding', myLayer)
  * view.pickObjectsAt({ x, y }, 'wfsBuilding', myObject3d)

It supports either layers, layer's id or THREE.Object3D.
By default it'll use THREE.Raycaster, but some layer can provide their own implementation.

Currently the layer with a custom implementation are:
  - layers using TileMesh (globe, planar, panorama)
  - pointclouds

author: Adrien Berthet <adrien.berthet@ign.fr>
message:
feat (core): complete and use FrameRequesters

This commit adds eight moments when a `FrameRequester` can be called in the
MainLoop :
- `UPDATE_START`
- `BEFORE_CAMERA_UPDATE`
- `AFTER_CAMERA_UPDATE`
- `BEFORE_LAYER_UPDATE`
- `AFTER_LAYER_UPDATE`
- `BEFORE_RENDER`
- `AFTER_RENDER`
- `UPDATE_END`

They can be used like this anywhere (at least where a view is reachable):
`view.addFrameRequester(itowns.View.BEFORE_CAMERA_UPDATE, frameRequester);`
where `frameRequester` is a function.

They are removed following a similar process:
`view.removeFrameRequester(itowns.View.BEFORE_CAMERA_UPDATE, frameRequester);`.

In the MainLoop, they are triggered each time (according to where they
belong) using
`view.execFrameRequesters(itowns.View.BEFORE_CAMERA_UPDATE);`.

Replace two cases where FrameRequesters weren't used, in `globe.js` with
`onAfterRender` and in `layersColorVisible.html` with `preRender`.
Adapt two cases where FrameRequesters were being used.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
fix(core): handle near pos. in box3 visibility functions

Projection matrix produces strange results when projecting a point behind
the camera near plane.
To avoid errors this commits clamp z coordinate to camera.near in camera space,
before projecting.

The issue can be tested in planar.html, by positionning the camera with:

    view.camera.camera3D.position.copy({x: 1841430.8707152607, y: 5173717.817231011, z: 229.93251060258268});
    view.camera.camera3D.rotation.set(-0.7231494579332582, -1.1919412510926017, -2.3305711080202998, "XYZ")
    view.notifyChange(true)

In this case box3SizeOnScreen used to return an y value between 0.91 and 1.3 while
the projected tile covers all the screen.

message:
feat(core): add vector tile loading in TMS

Vector tiles can be loaded in TMS as textures. Only Mapbox Vector Tile
is supported for now. This commit adds a new Parser (VectorTileParser),
and a new Helper (similar to OGCWebServiceHelper) VectorTileHelper.

Modifications have been done in Feature2Texture to support style as a
function, and as an object.

Also add two examples showing the use of Mapbox Vector Tiles in iTowns.
The first one is loading a full vector tile layer in a Planar view,
while the second only display national parks on top of a simple Ortho
layer in a a Globe view.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
Implement different layer update strategies

Add a configuration option to specify what kind of update strategy
is applied for a given level.

This commits implements 4:
  * STRATEGY_MIN_NETWORK_TRAFFIC: minimize network traffic by always
fetching the texture level matching node's level. This is the default
strategy.
  * STRATEGY_GROUP: maps level to groups. This effectively reduces the
granularity of a given layer. Was previously implemented in TileMesh
for elevation.
  * PROGRESSIVE: this strategy progressively refine level. Increment is
configurable (default: 1)
  * DICHOTOMY: is a special case of PROGRESSIVE.

author: Adrien Berthet <adrien.berthet@ign.fr>
message:
fix(label): correctly hide dom

There was a problem for a specific situation. Let's consider that there
is a level 2 node, with four level 3 nodes. The L2 node contains no
DOM elements, while there are some in the L3 nodes. So the DOM in L3
have no parents, they are the first in the hierarchy.  So if we find L2
hidden, we don't go further, and thus inside L3 nodes, and don't hide
the DOM.

This commit fixes this behaviour, by allowing to go further in the
hierarchy until DOM elements are found.

author: pierre-eric <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
feat (core): only use threeJsLayer feature when necessary

Using three.js' layers visibility has a big drawback: we're limited to 31 visibility
groups.
It's quite a low amount, so this commit changes the approach used for visibility:
  - GeometryLayer uses 'layer.object3d.visible' instead
  - layers attached to GeomLayer (like the TileDebug one) still use threeJsLayer,
    because their elements are attached to another layer's objects so they don't
    all share a common parent

Another change included is that now it doesn't make sense to use view.scene as a
default object3d parameter, so this commit switches to a Group instead.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
Refactor source layers and WMTS_Provider

With this change, (data source) layers are only known by the Quadtree.
They are used as an argument to Command instead of having the Provider
aware of them.
This allow several simplifications:
   * a single Provider (e.g WMTS_Provider) instance can be used, since data (layer)
   and processing (network fetch, parsing) are now decoupled
   * downsampling logic can be moved to NodeProcess (for now) instead of living in a
   Provider. This will help reusing the same logic with other data source.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
Refactor source layers and WMTS_Provider

With this change, (data source) layers are only known by the Quadtree.
They are used as an argument to Command instead of having the Provider
aware of them.
This allow several simplifications:
   * a single Provider (e.g WMTS_Provider) instance can be used, since data (layer)
   and processing (network fetch, parsing) are now decoupled
   * downsampling logic can be moved to NodeProcess (for now) instead of living in a
   Provider. This will help reusing the same logic with other data source.

author: Mathieu Brédif <mathieu.bredif@ign.fr>
message:
refactor(renderer): LayeredMaterial splitted and simplified

Worid has been fone to simplify LayeredMaterial and its surrounding
parts, especially with the management of textures in shaders.

LayeredMaterial has been splitted, and has now a LayeredMaterialLayer
property: this object will contain the textures linked to the material,
and uniforms related to each material.

Uniforms from LayeredMaterial are no longer accessible as is, and should
be accessible with directly using the uniform name. The material does
not do a lot of things, apart attaching a layer to it and managing
uniforms.

TileMesh has been simplified, removing all accessors in favor of direct
access to its properties. Material operations that were executed in it
have also been removed.

Shaders have been rewritten to reflect change quoted above. In an
attempt to simplify things and make them more comprehensible, TileFS and
TileVS have been splitted in multiple chunks, which are installed
through ShaderChunk.install.

BREAKING CHANGES: the API of TileMesh and LayeredMaterial have changed.
BREAKING CHANGES: LayeredMaterialConstants and RendererConstant have
been removed.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
refactor: deep rework of layers and threejs integration

See issues #217, #124, #40 for related discussion.

This massive commit:
  * unifies layers handling (geometry layers are no longer special citizen)
  * split processing in smaller units: these units will be more easy to reuse. For
example implementing Plane support will be easier because we're now able to share
the Tile and LayeredMaterial concepts without being forced to use Globe based
concept (e.g horizontalCulling).
  * limits the duplication of feature between three.js and iTowns: we get the best
of three.js and we remove incoherencies (e.g our Node were slightly different)
  * breaks the Globe|Quadtree centric vision of iTowns to ease the implementation of
other types of vizualisaiotn (oriented images, plane mode, pointcloud, etc)

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
fix(3dtiles): dont stop subdivision at tileset boundaries

In this scenario:
  - a tileset references an external tileset at node N
  - the subdivision algorithm decides to stop at N and display N
We must go one step further and display the content of the root
node R from the external tileset.

The reason is that R and N are the same node regarding content,
but are stored in different tilesets (for technical reasons)  and
thus considered as different node in iTowns (with N having R as
its only child).

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
Implement different layer update strategies

Add a configuration option to specify what kind of update strategy
is applied for a given level.

This commits implements 4:
  * STRATEGY_MIN_NETWORK_TRAFFIC: minimize network traffic by always
fetching the texture level matching node's level. This is the default
strategy.
  * STRATEGY_GROUP: maps level to groups. This effectively reduces the
granularity of a given layer. Was previously implemented in TileMesh
for elevation.
  * PROGRESSIVE: this strategy progressively refine level. Increment is
configurable (default: 1)
  * DICHOTOMY: is a special case of PROGRESSIVE.

Priority:
 * subdivision
 * uncomplete tiles
 * tiles meant to be displayed
 * others

The priority doesn't use sse or displayed attributes but instead prioritize
by category of command.
'sse' values for instance are meaningless as soon as the camera move/zoom so
comparing commands sse values doesn't help.

author: gchoqueux <gerald.choqueux@ign.fr>
message:
refactor(renderer): LayeredMaterial splitted and simplified

Worid has been fone to simplify LayeredMaterial and its surrounding
parts, especially with the management of textures in shaders.

LayeredMaterial has been splitted, and has now a LayeredMaterialLayer
property: this object will contain the textures linked to the material,
and uniforms related to each material.

Uniforms from LayeredMaterial are no longer accessible as is, and should
be accessible with directly using the uniform name. The material does
not do a lot of things, apart attaching a layer to it and managing
uniforms.

TileMesh has been simplified, removing all accessors in favor of direct
access to its properties. Material operations that were executed in it
have also been removed.

Shaders have been rewritten to reflect change quoted above. In an
attempt to simplify things and make them more comprehensible, TileFS and
TileVS have been splitted in multiple chunks, which are installed
through ShaderChunk.install.

BREAKING CHANGES: the API of TileMesh and LayeredMaterial have changed.
BREAKING CHANGES: LayeredMaterialConstants and RendererConstant have
been removed.

author: Adrien Berthet <adrien.berthet@ign.fr>
message:
fix(label): correctly hide dom

There was a problem for a specific situation. Let's consider that there
is a level 2 node, with four level 3 nodes. The L2 node contains no
DOM elements, while there are some in the L3 nodes. So the DOM in L3
have no parents, they are the first in the hierarchy.  So if we find L2
hidden, we don't go further, and thus inside L3 nodes, and don't hide
the DOM.

This commit fixes this behaviour, by allowing to go further in the
hierarchy until DOM elements are found.

author: Thomas Broyer <t.broyer@ltgt.net>
message:
Move from AMD and CommonJS to ES6 modules

With the exception of configuration, this is an almost-entirely
automated process:

    npm install amd-to-es6 esnext
    # Unname AMD modules
    sed -i "s|define.'[^']*'\s*,\s*|define(|g" \
        $(git grep --name-only  -e "define[(]'[^']*'\s*,")
    # Convert AMD modules to ES6 modules
    amdtoes6 -d src/ -o src/ -b
    # Convert CommonJS modules to ES6 modules
    find src/ -type f -name "*.js" \
        -not -name "*.min.js" -not -name "optimer_regular.js" \
        -exec esnext -I -w modules.commonjs {} \;
    # JS-Beautify output
    find src/ -type f -name "*.js" \
        -not -name "*.min.js" -not -name "optimer_regular.js" \
        -exec js-beautify -n -r {} \;
    # Remove dependencies
    npm uninstall amd-to-es6 esnext

Manual changes afterwards involved removing unused imports (ESLint
chokes on them as 'unused-vars') and re-formatting a number using
scientific notation that js-beautify broke in Core/Math/CVML.js.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
refactor(core): change view.notifyChange semantics

This commit changes the semantics of view.notifyChange function to something more
useful:
  changeSource now drives layer update.

This implies that no changeSource -> no update.

'changeSource' can be either a layer, an object from a layer or the camera.

The signature also changed slightly:
   notifyChange(needsRedraw = false, changeSource = undefined)
becomes:
   notifyChange(changeSource = undefined, needsRedraw = true)

Some examples usage:
  - notifyChange(): the scene will be redraw, but no update will be performed. This
is useful if a user adds some objetcs to the scene and wants to request a redraw but
do no need a full update of all layer (eg: a measure tool drawn with threejs lines)
  - notifyChange(XXX): only the layer XXX (or the layer to which XXX belongs) will
be updated. So if you have 100 layers, and layer #4 has a new texture, it will not
cause a full update of other layers.
  - notifyChange(camera): this is equivalent to the previous notifyChange(true): all
layers will be updated.

MainLoop also handles changeSource filtering and could later even handle ancestor
lookup (if we build a common ancestor lookup interface).

This actually moves a debug feature into core: it replaces `debugColor`
and `useDebugColor` with `customColor` and `useCustomColor`.

I think it is a useful feature to have in a production context:
- users can have several pointclouds displayed at the same time, and
  it's convenient to allow to separate them visually.
- When clouds have neither information of color nor intensity,

  have any on itowns right now, but for example Eye-Dome lightning add
  some black outlines. You can't see them if the cloud is black too.

message:
feat(core): add a Parser registry

Following #723 and the model of Providers, a Parser registry has been
partially added to the Scheduler. You can now register a Parser using
scheduler.addFormatParser(formatName, parser).

In the Scheduler queue, the Parser will be called right after the
Provider. It takes the datablob returned by the Provider, parses it, and
return it.

The parser selection relies on the format setted in the layer. For
layers that don't have a format, or have a format that is not supported,
a fake parser, returning immediatly the blob, is setted.

This commit introduces three parsers: GeoJson, Gpx and Kml. This allows
to refactor a bit the RasterProvider, in hope of letting go of it in the
future.

BREAKING CHANGE: GpxParser doesn't return a THREE.Mesh anymore.

author: Gerald Choqueux <gerald.choqueux@ign.fr>
message:
refactor(core): use common geometry in meshTile

 * identical geometries are reused to build the tileMeshs
 * the bounding boxes is calculated by THREE.js
 * bounding boxes can use the Parent's worldMatrix (tile).

BREAKING CHANGE
The geodesic normal in the center of the tile's geometry is aligned with the mesh's local Z axis.
Previously, the tiles were not oriented. their local landmark had the same orientation as the world landmark. You must take into account the orientation of the tile if you add objects to this tile.

Fixes:
 * Ellipsoid tile: The tile's geometry normal is computed with correct geodesic normal
 * reduces obb calculation errors see #87 issues
 * errors obb/culling for pano tile

Performance
 * the processes time (to build tiles in TileProvider.executeCommand) and used memory (geometryTile) are divided by ~3

message:
feat (3dtiles): use different subdiv. logic for add and sub refinement

This commit changes the way additive refinement is handled for 3dtiles.
Until now we had a single option: when a tile reached its sse threshold,
we would download and display all of its children.

In the additive refinement we can do better and only download the children
that will be visible. This reduces network/mem usage, for the same visual
result.

author: Alexandre Devaux <heythatsme@gmail.com>
message:
Max Texture in shader for Angle #86

Last Master 37df30d doesn't work on configuration Win + Angle because
shader GlobeFS.glsl tries to parse up to 16 textures
(else if (id == 15) return texture2D(dTextures[15],
pitUV(uv,pitScale_L01[15]));
But in LayerMaterial.js is defined:
var maxTexturesUnits = gfxEngine().glParams.maxTexturesUnits;
which is 16 like on most configuration and it is then decremented,
ending at 15.
It works if we keep maxTexturesUnits for pit and texture arrays.
But it shows a warning from ThreeJS: WebGLRenderer: trying to use 16
texture units while this GPU supports only 16

author: Augustin Trancart <augustin.trancart@oslandia.com>
message:
Chore: deduplicate dependencies between itowns.js and debug.js

If you import things somewhere in bundles itowns.js AND debug.js,
corresponding files (and all their deps) are getting bundled twice.
Apart from the extra size, this can cause bugs when some deps (eg.
three.js) expects you to include them only once (for id counting for
instance).

This commit removes deps that are already in itowns.js from debug.js.
One consequences is that we need to include debug.js after itowns.js.

In the future, it would be good to also extract a vendor.js bundle.

fix(core): implement preSSE once and fix the formula

3dTilesProcessing and GlobeTileProcessing use the same wrong SSE formula.

PR #633 and #818 proposed to fix this, but wasn't merged.

This commit fixes the computation, and comment it so the details should
be clearer and less dependant on an external reference that might go away.

The fixed bug can be seen easily in the oriented image example: if you
zoom in, the moutains behind the photos loses precision instead of increase it.

This should be fixed, and I added a unit test for this problem.

BREAKING CHANGE: Computing screen space error is changed, so tile subdivision are different.

author: pierre-eric <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
feat(core): implement layer priorities

Before this commit, commands issued by layers were stored per-host.
These commands queues are sorted by commands priority.

The problem caused by this design is that commands priority values
are not normalized and if 2 different types of layer (eg: color and pointcloud)
shared the same host, their commands ended up in the same queue.
Their ordering would be determined by comparing "apples and oranges": color
layer priorities are not comparable to pointcloud layer priorities.

To address this problem, this commit introduces 1 queue per layer
within the same host and adds an optional layer priority.

When the scheduler has an empty slot for a given host, it will first
select the layer (based on their relative priorities) and then pick
its top most command.

message:
examples: add anaglyph, parallax and stereo effects

Add three effects to display the scene in 3D. The first one is the
Anaglyph:
https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/dev/examples/js/effects/AnaglyphEffect.js
The second one is the Parallax:
https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/dev/examples/js/effects/ParallaxBarrierEffect.js
The last one is the Stereo effect, working only on a 3D-ready screen:
https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/dev/examples/js/effects/StereoEffect.js

To enable these effects, three methods are available:
- enableAnaglyph, for the first effect
- enableParallax, for the second
- enableStereo for Stereo

disableEffect can also be used for turning off an effect.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
test: use puppeteer to test all examples

This commit replaces the itowns-testing.js hack with puppeteer (https://github.com/GoogleChrome/puppeteer).

Advantages:
  - a real browser (Chrome) instead of node + mocks for missing features
  - WebGL capable
  - Can take screenshots and save them (not used on Travis yet)
  - Debuggable using Chrome Dev tools (Chrome instance used by puppeteer can be headless or not)

Each example now have at least one test to verify we can open it and that it
reaches the "mainloop has finished running" state.

I also implemented a couple tests for other examples (see 3dtiles and globe).

Adding test is easy, and we could add more to exercise more parts of itowns.

Last but not least: with this change the separation of examples in 2 files (html + js) is
not needed anymore.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
refactor: deep rework of layers and threejs integration

See issues #217, #124, #40 for related discussion.

This massive commit:
  * unifies layers handling (geometry layers are no longer special citizen)
  * split processing in smaller units: these units will be more easy to reuse. For
example implementing Plane support will be easier because we're now able to share
the Tile and LayeredMaterial concepts without being forced to use Globe based
concept (e.g horizontalCulling).
  * limits the duplication of feature between three.js and iTowns: we get the best
of three.js and we remove incoherencies (e.g our Node were slightly different)
  * breaks the Globe|Quadtree centric vision of iTowns to ease the implementation of
other types of vizualisaiotn (oriented images, plane mode, pointcloud, etc)

author: Thomas Broyer <t.broyer@ltgt.net>
message:
Fix concurrency bug in ProjectiveTexturingMaterial.init()

In case init() is called a second time before the it has resolved,
it now returns the same (unresolved) promise instead of a resolved
promise of 'null' (because _shaderMat wouldn't have been initialized

message:
chore(test): move variables declaration in describe()

In some unit tests, variables were declared before the first
`describe()` section of the file. When calling `npm run test-unit`, all
files are loaded and executed at the same time, with all `describe`
content being moved to a queue. So this causes a problem with things
declared before `describe`: a lot of variables (noticeably `context`)
were being rewritten and shared between all tests. While all tests were
passing, some of them would be false positive.
Moving all those declarations in `describe` fixes this.

author: Augustin Trancart <augustin.trancart@oslandia.com>
message:
Change import path from absolute to relative

This change is a necessary step to allow client code to import our
modules directly.

To achieve this, I used a little python script. I also had to change
some import orders to make the linter happy.

Work on generating lib/ and inlining glsl will be done in a subsequent
commit.

For reference, here is the python script:

import glob
import os
import re
import fileinput

prefix=os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'src')
list = ('Core', 'Globe', 'MobileMapping', 'Renderer', 'Scene')

for filename in glob.glob(prefix + '/**/*.js', recursive=True):
    for line in fileinput.input(filename, inplace=True):
        # check if local import
        if line.startswith('import ') and any(word in line for word in list):
            search = re.search('import (.*) from \'(.*)\';', line)
            if search:
                # importing a js
                importString = search.group(1)
                import_abs_path = os.path.join(prefix, search.group(2))
                import_rel_path = os.path.relpath(import_abs_path, os.path.dirname(filename))
                if not import_rel_path.startswith('.'):
                    # webpack needs ./ before relative path
                    import_rel_path = './' + import_rel_path
                print('import ' + importString + ' from \'' + import_rel_path + '\';')
            else:
                # importing something else
                print(line, end='')
        else:
            # import from node_modules
            print(line, end='')

message:
feat(core): compute TMS coordinates from top to bottom

As it can be read in the link at the end, TMS coordinates differ from
other "TMS" coordinates from Google Maps, OSM, Bing etc... The first one
goes from bottom to top, while the latter top to bottom. In this
commit, the parameter bottomLeft in the method computeTMSCoordinates
can be set to true to obtain the same result as Google Maps and others.

Source:
https://alastaira.wordpress.com/2011/07/06/converting-tms-tile-coordinates-to-googlebingosm-tile-coordinates/

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
refactor: store all node's textures in texture-atlas

Texture atlas usually perform better than individual textures.
It also allows to reduce the number of Sampler2D to the number of layer,
instead of the number of textures.

I didn't merged all the layers in a single atlas, because updating this
huge texture is slow (at least using the naive way of building a THREE.Texture
from an atlas. It may be feasible to access directly WebGL functions like
glTexSubImage2D).

Currently the texture packer is naive and probably only works for our test
data, but it should be easy to implement a more robust solution.
We could also consider modifying the AtlasBuilder to fit more textures in the
same atlas - not necessarly textures from the same tiles.

Last but not least, without this commit iTowns crashes on my phone :)

author: Adrien Berthet <berthet.a@gmail.com>
message:
feat(style): add Style inheritance

It is now possible to specify a `Style` parent for another `Style`. That
way, it is possible to define a global `Style` for a `ColorLayer`, while
defining one with property specific to a `FeatureGeometry` for example.
The `Style` of the `FeatureGeometry` will then only have the minimum
requirement, and it will read missing properties from its parent. It is
a dynamic reading, so it the parent values are changing, it is changing
as well for the child style.

This is a proposition for improvement in #1318.

BREAKING CHANGE: `Style#text.halo` is not available anymore, and each
property of it as been place in the `text` object, with the `halo`
prefix: `haloWidth`, `haloColor` and `haloBlur`.

author: Pierre-Eric Pelloux-Prayer <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
refactor: store all node's textures in texture-atlas

Texture atlas usually perform better than individual textures.
It also allows to reduce the number of Sampler2D to the number of layer,
instead of the number of textures.

I didn't merged all the layers in a single atlas, because updating this
huge texture is slow (at least using the naive way of building a THREE.Texture
from an atlas. It may be feasible to access directly WebGL functions like
glTexSubImage2D).

Currently the texture packer is naive and probably only works for our test
data, but it should be easy to implement a more robust solution.
We could also consider modifying the AtlasBuilder to fit more textures in the
same atlas - not necessarly textures from the same tiles.

Last but not least, without this commit iTowns crashes on my phone :)

author: pierre-eric <pierre-eric.pelloux-prayer@oslandia.com>
message:
refactor(core): unify mesh picking methods

The idea of this PR is to expose a single entry point for querying the view.

This method belongs to the View.

Here are a few example usage:
  * view.pickObjectsAt({ x, y })
  * view.pickObjectsAt({ x, y }, 'wfsBuilding')
  * view.pickObjectsAt({ x, y }, 'wfsBuilding', myLayer)
  * view.pickObjectsAt({ x, y }, 'wfsBuilding', myObject3d)

It supports either layers, layer's id or THREE.Object3D.
By default it'll use THREE.Raycaster, but some layer can provide their own implementation.

Currently the layer with a custom implementation are:
  - layers using TileMesh (globe, planar, panorama)
  - pointclouds

message:
feat(core): add the ability to colorize pointclouds

This actually moves a debug feature into core: it replaces `debugColor`
and `useDebugColor` with `customColor` and `useCustomColor`.

I think it is a useful feature to have in a production context:
- users can have several pointclouds displayed at the same time, and
  it's convenient to allow to separate them visually.
- When clouds have neither information of color nor intensity,
  colorizing them allows to see applied visual improvements. We don't
  have any on itowns right now, but for example Eye-Dome lightning add
  some black outlines. You can't see them if the cloud is black too.

author: Adrien Berthet <adrien.berthet@ign.fr>
message:
feat(core): compute TMS coordinates from top to bottom

As it can be read in the link at the end, TMS coordinates differ from
other "TMS" coordinates from Google Maps, OSM, Bing etc... The first one
goes from bottom to top, while the latter top to bottom. In this
commit, the parameter bottomLeft in the method computeTMSCoordinates
can be set to true to obtain the same result as Google Maps and others.

Source:
https://alastaira.wordpress.com/2011/07/06/converting-tms-tile-coordinates-to-googlebingosm-tile-coordinates/
https://wiki.osgeo.org/wiki/Tile_Map_Service_Specification
https://www.planet.com/docs/reference/tile-services
